messages:
eli: Quick sync0min: customers are confused when our usage table shows their project but the actual service account that ran the inference is invisible.
shanice: Is this a billing problem or just debugging UX?
eli: Mostly UX and alerts. Billing still charges the billed project correctly, but alert rules and usage filters point at the wrong identity.
tom: Suggestion: auth-proxy emit a sealed header `X-RW-Effective` with final principal; runtime can plumb into traces + metrics.
irene: We need privacy gating in the console. If someone doesn't have access to that SA's project we should not expose the SA name.
shanice: Cardinality note: SAs are numerous and short-lived in some orgs. We must ensure adding a metric tag doesn't blow up our TSDB.
sre-bot: Reminder: any new metric dimension requires cardinality analysis and an opt-out for billing ETL.
tom: Implementation sketch: 1) header behind flag; 2) attach to spans and metering message as optional `effective_principal`; 3) store top-K per org, bucket the rest as `sa:other`.
irene: UI: add toggle "group by effective principal" on usage table and an access check. Default remains grouping by origin to avoid noise.
eli: Rollout plan: emit header for 72h behind flag, collect counts, then enable console column behind a feature flag. Alerts by effective principal are opt-in.
shanice: Also capture `impersonation_chain_len` metric so we can detect nested proxies.
tom: Security: proxy must sign header or we validate via mTLS to prevent spoofing.
sre-bot: RFC required: impersonation-observability. Please include a 30d sample cardinality report.
irene: I'll mock the console overlay and privacy copy. eli: I'll coordinate with billing to ensure no ETL impacts. Ping #eng-oncall if alerts spike during the probe window. :thumbsup:
